correctness.rationale: The normalization is precisely T=(S⊗S*+S*⊗S)/2 and the one-spike coefficients are a/2 at the two ends of every homogeneous block of size at least three. Reflection gives the exact symmetric/antisymmetric split. For |lambda|>1 the interior free resolvent is explicitly g=2U_(m-1)/U_m and h=2/U_m; the scalar Schur-complement equations converge uniformly to lambda−(a²/2)rho. Solving the root equation yields only ±a²/(2sqrt(a²−1)) with |rho|<1 exactly when a>sqrt(2). Disjoint interior reflected plane waves prove all of [-1,1] belongs to each essential spectrum, and reflected exponentially decaying half-line eigenvectors give Weyl sequences at both detached points. All boundaries a>0 and a=sqrt(2) are included; finitely many low-degree sections are correctly ignored for essential spectra. The delivered standalone script passed 2,371 finite algebra and matrix tests; infinite statements are proved analytically, not inferred from those tests.

originality.rationale: The source-matched claim concerns Fredholm essential spectral accumulation for a positive one-spike weighted shift in both tensor-symmetry sectors. Garcia–O'Loughlin–Yu Theorem 8.1 establishes only the unweighted case and their Problem 7 asks for weighted shifts. Tian–Wang–Zhu Theorem 1.3 addresses norm identities, not this essential-spectrum transition. Yang–Zhang Theorem 3.3 gives characteristic-polynomial descriptions of each finite homogeneous-block point spectrum, which subsumes the block reduction but does not state or immediately evaluate the uniform-block essential-spectrum limit or spike threshold. The proof supplies new boundary-resolvent asymptotics and parity-separated singular Weyl sequences. Exact searches of published mathematical records and accessible earlier scientific-claim records found no dominating specific statement; this is a best-knowledge rather than independently certified novelty judgment.

The Webb–Olver 2021 article was not inspected in full, so no whole-document exclusion is asserted; its general Jacobi methods may overlap proof ingredients.
Definitive priority and independent correctness have not been established.

value.rationale: The one-spike family is a canonical compact perturbation of the unilateral shift in an open weighted-shift tensor-spectral problem. The theorem completely describes both Fredholm essential spectra and exact essential norms for the entire parameter range, with a sharp threshold and two isolated essential outliers. It reveals that rank-one perturbation of the underlying shift can create new essential spectrum after tensor construction, and that both tensor symmetries have the same limiting phase transition despite different finite sections. The closed threshold and quadratic onset are structurally motivated; these are not arbitrary finite table entries or a routine substitute for the general theory.
